.claude\rules\codification-threshold.md:68:Codifying too early costs LOC in a reference file (~50-150 LOC typical). Codifying too late costs re-derive time at each future application. For patterns where re-derive is cheap (~minutes), waiting for n=2 is effectively free. For patterns where re-derive is expensive (>15 min), every "wait for n=2" burns 15+ min on the next application — and if frequency is several per month, the wait dominates.

.claude\rules\audit-action-loop.md:123:Audit-failure is the worst defect class: a broken audit looks like it's working (entries appear in JSONL) while providing 0 protection. Worse: a working audit that surfaces drift but isn't actioned has the same effect — the mechanization runs, the data accumulates, but nothing closes the drift. Within 12-24h of accumulation, drift becomes "background noise" that humans/agents stop checking. The audit-action-loop is the consumer-side discipline that makes wired audits valuable.
